title: Conferences / Pre-Trial Conferences / Case Conferences
coreDoctrine: Rule 50 is not mere scheduling. It is a trial-readiness, settlement, issue-narrowing, expert-readiness, and court-management system.
authoritySectionsCaptured: RCP50:1 Synopsis, Comment and Advocacy Notes

forms.purpose: Concise pre-trial brief with required Rule 50.04 contents
Report under Rule 50.08 with steps, timing, trial length, readiness certification

deadlineObjects.name: PreTrialSchedulingWindow
deadlineObjects.deadline: For actions set down after March 30, 2022, pre-trial conference generally scheduled not more than 120 days and not less than 30 days before the later of trial date or first sitting date, unless order/practice direction provides otherwise.

deadlineObjects.name: CertificateOfReadinessDeadline
deadlineObjects.deadline: At least 30 days before pre-trial conference.

deadlineObjects.name: PreTrialBriefDeadline
deadlineObjects.deadline: At least 5 days before pre-trial conference, with proof of service.

decisionTrees.name: PreTrialReadiness
logic: Confirm action/application and whether pre-trial conference is mandatory or court-directed.
Confirm Form 50A delivered at least 30 days before pre-trial.
Confirm expert reports served or reasons for non-service captured.
Confirm pre-trial brief filed with proof of service at least 5 days before pre-trial.
After conference, generate trial readiness tasks and certification obligations.

decisionTrees.name: PreTrialConfidentiality
logic: Do not communicate pre-trial statements to hearing judge/officer except as disclosed in Rule 50.07 order or Rule 50.08 report.
Flag risk if user tries to include pre-trial settlement statements in trial materials.

decisionTrees.name: PreTrialJudgeConflict
logic: If judge conducted pre-trial conference, do not assign same judge to trial/hearing unless all parties consent in writing.
Conference before trial judge during hearing does not automatically disqualify under Rule 50.10(2).

crossRuleDependencies.relationship: Settlement offers and settlement authority feed pre-trial settlement discussions.
Expert report service is directly checked in Form 50A / Rule 50.03.1.
Unproductive pre-trial conduct can trigger costs.
Pre-trial powers may include orders under Rule 20.05 after unsuccessful summary judgment motion.
Separate hearings/bifurcation intention must be addressed; order may require consent.
Case conference can connect to Rule 77 case management proceedings.

codingImplementationNotes: Rule 50 must feed TrialReadinessEngine and not be coded as simple calendar scheduling.
Pre-trial readiness must check experts, witnesses, admissions, issues, trial length, documents, settlement authority, and unfinished steps.
Confidential pre-trial communications must be protected from trial materials unless captured in formal order/report.
Pre-trial report must update MasterCaseSchema with trial readiness obligations and fixed-date readiness certification.
Rule 50 is a bridge between settlement strategy, trial preparation, expert evidence, costs risk, and judicial case management.
